ideas.title: Putting over buried magnet stones
ideas.critique: Sprinkling iron sand to read a hidden green turns the ironsand still into a game you replay, and a ball curling or stalling on a field nobody placed is new. The risk is the numbers: an induced moment's force falls off very steeply, and a lodestone under sand barely moves an iron ball rolling on grass. Unless the stone is centimetres from the line, honest physics gives a ball that rolls straight, and a bent coefficient would make this the same rig as before.

ideas.title: The stone-and-ball cannon
ideas.critique: This is the well-known magnet-and-balls cannon, so anyone who has seen one can predict the shot, and a lodestone's honest exit speed is a gentle roll that will hardly topple a tower. Its strength is that magnetic energy becomes motion through solved contacts and the soft-iron chain, and that a badly built cannon really just clacks.
